 along with petitioners in pe  versus  THE STATE (NCT OF DELHI) & ANR. ..... Resp  Through: Mr.Shoaib Haider, APP with  Beena  Mr.Rana Kunal, Mr.Apoorv  Malik, Ms.Shivani Mehta a  Mr.Manoj Kr. Rana, Advs. 
 R-2 along with R-2 in per  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NAVIN CHAWLA  ORDER % 13.05.2024 1.

This petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short,
'Cr.P.C.') seeking quashing of FIR No.313/2021 registered at Police Station: Sector-23 Dwarka,
Dwarka District, Delhi under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short,
'IPC'), along with all other proceedings arising therefrom, on the basis of settlement.
2. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the subject FIR was an offshoot of the matrimonial discord between the parties, that is, the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2.
He further submits that no child is born from the wedlock of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2.

sentences.text: He submits that the parties have, now, amicably settled their inter se disputes and have entered into a settlement vide Mutual Agreement dated 21.09.2021.

He submits that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have already filed a petition seeking the dissolution of their marriage by mutual consent before the learned Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Yamuna Nagar, Bilaspur,
District Yamuna Nagar, Haryana.

entities.text:
Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Yamuna Nagar, Bilaspur,
District Yamuna Nagar, Haryana
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The respondent no.2, who appears in person and has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer (IO), reaffirms the above- mentioned settlement and states that she has settled all the disputes with the petitioners out of her own free will and without any coercion.
She submits that she has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
The respondent no.2 further states that she will also withdraw the litigation that has been filed by her before the Court at Yamuna Nagar, Haryana against the petitioners.
5. I have perused the contents of the FIR and also the Settlement between the parties.

6. Keeping in view the fact that the disputes between the parties arose out of a matrimonial relationship, and now the same have been amicably settled, and also looking into the nature of the allegations made in the complaint, in my opinion, no useful purpose would be served in keeping the FIR alive.
In fact, it would rather create further acrimony between the parties and will be an unnecessary burden on the State Exchequer.
7. Guided by the principles enunciated by the Supreme Court in its judgments in Jitendra Raghuvanshi v. Babita Raghuvanshi, (2013) 4 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

Ors. v. Bhajan Lal & Ors. 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, this Court deems it appropriate, in the interest of justice, to exercise its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR and all the proceedings emanating therefrom.

, and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom against the petitioners are quashed.
9. The pending application is also disposed of as being rendered infructuous.
